MAJOR: Schema truth is derived by regex-parsing `*.up.sql` (`_schema`, `_statements_after`): columns added via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`, quoted/mixed-case identifiers, inline constraints, and comments will be mis-parsed. A gate that decides "migrated" from brittle text scanning will both false-fail and false-pass; introspect the applied database (or migrations tool metadata) instead.

`migration_status` semantics were loosened in bulk: ~80 stores flip `pending`→`migrated` purely because a `CREATE TABLE` line exists in some migration file. "migrated" now means "a DDL statement exists", not "data lives there / migration applied". This overstates readiness and will mislead capacity, DR, and compliance planning.

The registry content does not match what `--apply` produces: apply() preserves `kind: table` targets and injects `retained_reason`, but the diff hand-rewrites those entries to `kind: file`/`retained` with empty `ref`/`owner_item`. The `retained_reason` branch in `_expected_status` is dead code, and the next `--apply` run's behavior versus this hand state is unverified — registry edits must go through the tool, not around it.

Canonical edge set is hardcoded twice (SEED in the shipped tool + JSON in the registry), and `check` fails on any "unexpected canonical relationship". Adding a domain relationship (the stated Slice C purpose) now requires editing shipped tooling code, inverting the AC's intent. The tool should own validation rules; the registry should own the edge catalog.

Deleting `reason` from retained-file targets and substituting empty `"ref": "", "owner_item": ""` fields is pure information loss: the audit rationale ("global authored config -> file (git-reviewed)") is gone, replaced by two no-op empty strings. Empty-string required fields also defeat the "planned targets must name an owner" invariant by satisfying presence-checks with nulls.
MINOR: `_item_status` swallows every exception into `"unknown"`, which then hard-fails the gate — a missing/renamed backlog item file breaks CI with a misleading message; narrow the except and distinguish "missing" from "unreadable".

Hardcoded `REQUIRED_TRIGGERS`, `OBJECT_META` (`{"artifacts","stored_objects"}`), and the table/backend allow-lists embed current-state knowledge in shipped code; renaming a trigger or adding an object bucket breaks the fast gate for reasons unrelated to the change under review.

`_schema` ignores `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`, so any column added post-creation (indexes/audits/tombstones) is invisible to relationship validation — same root cause as the regex issue but worth an explicit tracked follow-up.
`KINDS` admits `"view"` while the AC enumerates table|file|derived|object-store; either the AC or the enum is wrong — align them so the gate enforces the accepted taxonomy.
Duplicate required-edge computation (`REQUIRED - set(canonical)` and `REQUIRED - set(all rels)`) emits two overlapping messages for one defect; consolidate for cleaner CI output.
`--verbose` is parsed and threaded to `_report`, which unconditionally prints every problem and ignores the flag — dead parameter.
NIT: `import glob` + `glob.glob` instead of `Path.glob`; the module already uses `path` objects everywhere else.
`--self-test` picks the "first" table store from the live registry to mutate; a fixed synthetic fixture would make the negative tests independent of registry churn.
`_statements_after` treats `"` and `'` identically when skipping quoted regions — a comment containing an apostrophe inside a migration can desync paren matching.
SUMMARY: Solid gate discipline (fail-closed checks, negative self-tests, wiring into precheck + ci-cd-gates), but the foundation — regex DDL parsing as schema truth and a hardcoded canonical edge set in shipped code — is fragile and will not scale past the next few domains.

Highest risks: mass `migration_status` flip to "migrated" based on DDL-text presence (overstates readiness), registry hand-edited in a state `--apply` would not reproduce (tool/state drift), and rationale-bearing `reason` fields replaced with empty strings (auditability loss).
Recommend: validate against real schema state, move the edge catalog fully into the registry, restore human-readable retention rationale, and re-derive the registry via `--apply` before merge.
